The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has emerged champions of the second edition of the CGF Cup 2026 after defeating the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps 5-3 on penalties in the final at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium, Abuja, on Saturday. The match ended goalless after regulation time before EFCC triumphed in the penalty shootout to claim the title. CGF Cup 2026, also called Comptroller-General Football Tournament, is the second edition of an inter-agency football competition in Nigeria organised by the Federal Fire Service for eight security, law enforcement, and emergency response agencies. The outcome was announced in a statement signed by the FFS’ National Public Relations Officer and Head of Corporate Services, DCF Paul Abraham, on Saturday. The Nigerian Air Force secured third position after defeating the Nigeria Correctional Service 3-1 in the third-place match. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Haruna Yakubu then scored twice to give the Air Force victory. The final kicked off at 3pm, with the Controller-General of the Federal Fire Service, Samuel Olumide, performing the ceremonial kick-off. He was accompanied by the Deputy Controllers-General, Achi Okidi and Kehinde Ajasa; Assistant Controller-General GK Arogundade; Chairman of the AMAC Football Committee, Otunba Paul Oluwole; directors of sports from participating security agencies; and other dignitaries. Following the final, Olumide presented individual awards to outstanding players and officials. Achem Ezekiel of the Federal Fire Service won the top scorer award after netting two goals in 45 minutes, while Titus Ayuba of NSCDC was named the Most Valuable Player. Eze Daniel of EFCC won the Best Goalkeeper award, while his team’s coach, Kabiru Sani, was named Best Coach. EFCC finished as champions, NSCDC as runners-up and the Nigerian Air Force in third place. The Federal Fire Service said the competition promoted unity, friendship and sportsmanship among security agencies, while strengthening inter-agency collaboration and institutional relationships.
